definitions.explanation: A characteristic Japanese flavor profile combining sweetness (often from sugar or mirin) with the savory saltiness of soy sauce. Typical of teriyaki, simmered dishes, and many sauces — not "sweet and spicy" despite the literal kanji.

examples.japanese: この{味|あじ}は{甘辛|あまから}い。
{甘辛|あまから}いタレを{肉|にく}にかけた。
examples.english: I poured the sweet-and-savory sauce over the meat.

examples.japanese: {甘辛|あまから}い{味付|あじつ}けは{白|しろ}ご{飯|はん}との{相性|あいしょう}が{抜群|ばつぐん}だ。
examples.english: A sweet-and-savory seasoning goes exceptionally well with plain rice.

notes:
Despite containing {辛|から}い (spicy/salty), this word almost always refers to the soy-sauce-and-sugar flavor of Japanese home cooking, not chili heat. Think teriyaki, sukiyaki broth, or simmered fish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘辛|あまから}いタレ: sweet-and-savory sauce
- {甘辛|あまから}い{味付|あじつ}け: sweet-and-savory seasoning
- {甘辛|あまから}い{煮物|にもの}: sweet-and-savory simmered dish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甘辛|あまから}: the noun form, used in compounds like {甘辛|あまから}{煮|に} (sweet-savory simmered dish)
- {甘酸|あまず}っぱい: sweet and sour — fruity tartness; very different flavor
- {辛|から}い: salty; spicy — covers both "hot" and "salty" in Japanese, but context usually makes it clear

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {甘辛|あまから}くなかったら
